Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-medium-0039-reverse-08", "row_sha256": "f37ae2120c432437465374f433f873546c6f18ef2bdbfc49785c3e66d7dce64f", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey, can you help me shape a short announcement for our neighborhood seed exchange? it's the spring swap organized by the Green Corner group, and it's happening saturday, may 18, from 10 a.m. to noon in the East Room at Maple Street Library. please make it clear that this is a community event hosted by the group, not a formal library program.

people can bring vegetable, herb, or flower seeds to share. ask them to put seeds in labeled packets if they can, but we’ll have some empty envelopes at the table too. nobody has to bring seeds to attend, and there’s no fee. mention that folks can take home seeds even if they don’t have any to trade. keep the wording welcoming and fairly brief, not like a big official notice. don’t add a registration link or say that the library is providing supplies; we only know the group has envelopes. send the finished announcement to Jasper, not Celeste. Jasper is helping pass it along to households on Birch and Alder streets, and Celeste isn’t handling invitations for this exchange. Could you organize those details into a usable prompt for writing the announcement?", "output": "Write a short, welcoming announcement for the Green Corner group’s neighborhood spring seed exchange. The event is on Saturday, May 18, from 10 a.m. to noon in the East Room at Maple Street Library. Make clear that it is a community event hosted by the group, not a formal library program.

Mention that people may bring vegetable, herb, or flower seeds to share. Ask them to use labeled packets if they can; the group will have some empty envelopes available. No one needs to bring seeds to attend, there is no fee, and attendees may take home seeds even if they have none to trade. Keep the announcement fairly brief and welcoming, not like a large official notice. Do not add a registration link or say that the library is providing supplies.

Send the finished announcement to Jasper, not Celeste. Jasper is helping pass it along to households on Birch and Alder streets, and Celeste is not handling invitations for this exchange."}]
